--- title: "Frequentist parameter estimation" course-unit: ch10-parameter-estimation status: complete julia: exeflags: ["--project=../../environments/ch10"] --- ## Why this unit matters - The observation models chapter produced case reports from a **known** process. - Now reverse the arrow: given only the reports, what are the parameters? - The **frequentist** view: parameters are fixed unknowns; uncertainty is the sampling behaviour of estimators. ::: {.notes} This deck runs in the isolated environment `environments/ch10`, pinned via the document's `julia.exeflags`, which carries mutually compatible `ProfileLikelihood`, `Optimization`, and `OrdinaryDiffEq` versions. ::: ## Model and likelihood Deterministic SIR ODE + Poisson observations, estimating $\theta=(i_0,\beta)$ with $c=10,\gamma=0.25$ fixed. Model incidence $x_t(\theta)$ gives the Poisson log-likelihood $$ \ell(\theta)=\sum_{t=1}^{n}\big[y_t\log x_t(\theta)-x_t(\theta)-\log(y_t!)\big]. $$ Profile out nuisance parameters and use Wilks' theorem for intervals: $$ \ell_p(\beta)=\max_{i_0}\ell(i_0,\beta),\qquad \text{95\% CI}:\ \ell_p(\beta)\ge\ell(\hat\theta)-1.92. $$ ::: {.notes} The threshold $1.92=\tfrac12\chi^2_{1,0.95}$ is the Venzon–Moolgavkar construction implemented by `ProfileLikelihood.jl`. ::: ## Fitting: MLE and profile intervals ::: {#cell-ch08-results .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#ch08-results .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Sample counts and grid are small so the deck runs quickly; a real profile would use a finer grid. ::: ## Profile log-likelihoods ::: {#cell-fig-slide-ch08-profile .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#fig-slide-ch08-profile .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Profile log-likelihoods for i₀ and β. Dashed line: 95% threshold; blue dotted: interval endpoints; red: truth. ::: ::: ::: {.notes} Each curve is normalised to zero at the MLE; the interval is where it lies above the dashed Wilks threshold. A flat profile would signal weak identifiability. ::: ## Takeaways and limitations - MLE via `Optimization.jl`; profile CIs via `ProfileLikelihood.jl`. - Nelder–Mead is **local** — use multistart before trusting one fit. - The $\chi^2$ calibration is **asymptotic**; small samples may mis-cover. - $\beta$ and $c$ enter only as $\beta c$ $\Rightarrow$ not separately identifiable (the sensitivity and identifiability chapter). - Intervals summarise sampling variability, not prior knowledge — the Bayesian inference chapter is the Bayesian counterpart. Read the [book chapter](../../chapters/10-parameter-estimation.html); see [Optimization.jl](https://docs.sciml.ai/Optimization/stable/) and [ProfileLikelihood.jl](https://github.com/DanielVandH/ProfileLikelihood.jl). ::: {.notes} Emphasise that "narrow interval" is a statement about this data-generating setup, not a guarantee that every biological parameter is learnable. :::
